question: Which State in India has the lowest population density?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• According to the **Census 2011**, **Arunachal Pradesh** has the lowest population density among all states in **India**, with only **17 persons per square kilometer**.

• The low population density is primarily due to the state's vast **geographical area** of **83,743 square kilometers** coupled with a relatively small **population** of approximately **1.38 million**.

• The **topography** of **Arunachal Pradesh**, characterized by the rugged **Eastern Himalayas**, deep valleys, and dense **forest cover** (over **80%** of its land), makes large parts of the state difficult to inhabit, leading to sparse settlements.

• Comparing the other options: **Sikkim** has a population density of **86**, **Nagaland** has **119**, and **Manipur** has **115** persons per square kilometer. While these are low compared to the national average, they are significantly higher than that of **Arunachal Pradesh**.

• The **Census 2011** was the **15th** official census of **India** and remains the primary source of **demographic data** used for administrative and planning purposes.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Highest Density State**: **Bihar** is the most densely populated state in **India** as per the **2011 Census**, with a density of **1,106 persons per square kilometer**.

• **National Average**: The overall **population density** of **India** was recorded at **382 persons per square kilometer** in **2011**, an increase from **325** in the **2001 Census**.

• **Union Territories**: Among **Union Territories**, **Delhi** has the highest population density at **11,320 persons per square kilometer**, while the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** have the lowest at **46**.

• **Least Populous State**: Although **Arunachal Pradesh** has the lowest density, **Sikkim** is the **least populous state** in **India** with a total population of about **6.11 lakh**.

• **Growth Trends**: **Nagaland** was the only state in **India** to show a **negative decadal growth rate** of **-0.58%** between **2001** and **2011**.

**Important Points__**

• **Definition**: **Population Density** is defined as the number of persons living per unit of area (usually per **square kilometer**). It is a key indicator of **population distribution** and **urbanization**.

• **District Level Data**: Within **Arunachal Pradesh**, the **Dibang Valley** district has the lowest density in the entire country, with only about **1 person per square kilometer**.

• **Geographical Significance**: **Arunachal Pradesh** is the largest state in **Northeast India** by area and is known as the **Land of the Rising Sun** because it receives the first **sunlight** in **India** at **Dong Valley**.

• **Census Authority**: The **Census** in **India** is conducted every **10 years** by the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**. The **2011 Census** was conducted under **C. Chandramouli**.
